sections.title: Currently shipped
entries: IPhreeqc / PHREEQC — USGS User Rights Notice (public-domain-like, U.S. Geological Survey). IPhreeqc is by S.R. Charlton and D.L. Parkhurst; PHREEQC is by D.L. Parkhurst and C.A.J. Appelo. Aqueous speciation, mineral saturation, gas partitioning and redox are built from the pinned vendored source and its thermodynamic databases (phreeqc.dat, wateq4f.dat, minteq.v4.dat and pitzer.dat). Kerotakis modifies the build integration and BASIC runtime; it is not an unmodified USGS distribution.
MY-BASIC — MIT, Copyright (c) 2011–2026 Tony Wang. Pinned language core for PHREEQC BASIC programs (rate expressions, user punch/print, calculated values). Default in all Kerotakis builds.

NASA CEA thermodynamic data and code — Apache-2.0, Copyright (c) 2025, United States Government as represented by the Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. The embedded `thermo.inp` supplies NASA-9 gas and condensed-phase thermochemistry.
diffsol — MIT, Copyright (c) Martin Robinson. Stiff ODE/DAE integration for reaction kinetics.
chematic — MIT OR Apache-2.0, authored by kent-tokyo. Structure parsing, reaction templates and the wasm-compatible molecular identity path.
Svelte — MIT, Copyright (c) 2016–2025 Svelte Contributors. User interface.

Rust crates and native-shell dependencies — licences include MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode, Unlicense and other expressions named in the bundled inventory. The in-app open-source licence document names every package, version, declared licence, authors and repository and reproduces each licence/notice file present in its package.

sections.title: Curated data
entries: Kerotakis-authored chemistry data shipped in official binaries (the codex: reactions, observations, register copy, colour and property curation) is licensed CC BY 4.0, separately from the AGPL-3.0 code. Imported CC0 records, including the oehTopics curriculum vocabulary, remain CC0 1.0 and name their source per record. No CC BY-SA data is bundled in official apps.

Where curated data incorporates or is checked against third-party datasets, those are named with their own terms per record — and where an upstream's licence claim appears inconsistent with its own sources, Kerotakis honours the original source's terms.

sections.title: Reactivity screening
entries: The reactive-group compatibility screen is Kerotakis' own implementation of the methodology published in open-access literature by NOAA's Office of Response and Restoration with the EPA and the Center for Chemical Process Safety. It does not contain or reproduce the CAMEO Chemicals database or any of its contributed proprietary fields.

sections.title: Reviewed ligand equilibrium constants
entries: U.S. Bureau of Mines IC 9429 (1995), Charles M. Flynn, Jr. and Sandra M. Haslem, Cyanide Chemistry — Precious Metals Processing and Waste Treatment. Six 25 °C, zero-ionic-strength complex formation constants transcribed from Tables D-7 and D-15. CDC Stacks explicitly identifies the report as Public Domain: https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/206360 . See the per-field review in provenance/usbm-ic9429-complexes-review.md. No spectra or rates are supplied.

sections.title: Reviewed hydrogen bromide gas uptake
entries: Rolf Sander (2023), Compilation of Henry's law constants (version 5.0.0) for water as solvent, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 23, 10901-12440, https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-23-10901-2023 . Copyright Author(s) 2023, licensed Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Only HBr note 146's reference constant and temperature slope are used. Changes: converted concentration/pressure units and derived a local reaction enthalpy using the USGS PHREEQC pure-water density formulation. No endorsement implied. See provenance/sander-2023-hbr-review.md for conditions and omissions.

sections.title: Reviewed additional-solvent distillation reference fields
entries: U.S. Coast Guard CHRIS manual (June 1999), methanol (MAL) and isopropanol (IPA), sections 9.2, 9.3 and 9.12: molar mass, normal boiling point and latent heat. U.S. government physical-property information; see https://www.uscg.mil/disclaim/ and the original NOAA-hosted manual PDFs https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/chris/MAL.pdf and https://cameochemicals.noaa.gov/chris/IPA.pdf . This narrow slice excludes third-party restricted categories and is not a CAMEO database export. Unit conversion and a bounded constant-latent ideal-mixture approximation are Kerotakis modifications, not government predictions or endorsement. See provenance/uscg-chris-still-review.md for the limits.

sections.title: Development and build-time tools (not distributed with app binaries)
entries: SUNDIALS/CVODE — BSD-3-Clause-style LLNL licence; Regents of the University of California / Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. Used only as a native differential test oracle through the `kerotakis-sundials` workspace crate, not linked into the released app.

The official IUPAC InChI library — MIT, Copyright (c) 2024 IUPAC and InChI Trust. Used behind the `native-inchi` validation feature; released apps use chematic's pure-Rust path and do not link the vendored C library.
